questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

She said to me, “I saw this old man long ago.”

options.text: She told me that she had seen that old man long before.
She told to me that she had seen that old man long before.
She said to me that she had seen that old man long ago.
She said me that she had seen this old man long ago.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'She told me that she had seen that old man long before.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the given question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• In the given sentence the reporting verb has an object. Hence, 'said to' will be changed into** 'told'. **
 
• Comma and inverted commas will be removed. 
 
• The conjunction 'that' will be added.
 
• '**I**' will be changed into '**she**' because the** first person pronouns** are changed according to the subject of the **reporting verb.**
 
• V2 will be changed into 'had + V3'. (simple past tense changes into past perfect tense)
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.

 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__ *She told me that she had seen that old man long before.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The booking will have been closed when you reach the theatre.

options.text: They would have closed the booking when you reach the theatre.
They had closed the booking when you reached the theatre.
They will have closed the booking when you reach the theatre.
They will close the booking when you reach the theatre.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'They will have closed the booking when you reach the theatre.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of Passive Voice. As per the given question we have to change it into Active Voice. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'The booking'.
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'they (hidden)'.
 
• Since modal verb has been used in the passive voice, therefore, the active voice will follow the given structure:
 
 
• Passive Voice - modal verb*(will)* + have + been + V3
 
• Active Voice - modal verb*(will) *+ have + V3
 
 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• 'will have been closed' will be changed into 'will have closed'.

 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__* They will have closed the booking when you reach the theatre.*

questions.question:

__Would you have been__ so kind as to close the window?

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'Would you be'** should be used instead of** 'Would you have been'.**
 
• We generally use the **modal verb** ‘**would**’ when we want to **politely request someone **for something. Hence, option 4 is incorrect.
 
 
• For example: **Would** you bring me a cup of coffee?
 
 
 
• Also, 'would' is a **modal**. A modal is always followed by the** V1 **form of verb.
 
 
• For example: Would you** do** it?
 
 
 
• Only 'be' among the options is in the **V1** form. The rest of the verbs in the other options are not in the V1 form.
 
• Hence, 'would you be' is the correct segment that must be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__ *****Would you be** so kind as to close the window?*

questions.question:
**Arrange the statements in the correct order to make a meaningful paragraph.**

A. Impressed with Jane’s patience with animals, he chose her for the mission to understand chimpanzees.

B. In 1957, she went to Kenya where she met the British paleoanthropologist, Louis Leakey.

C. As a child she would wait for hours to observe a chicken laying an egg.

D. Jane Goodall grew up in the English town of Bournemouth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**DCBA**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
 
• **Sentence D** will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence that tells us about 'Jane Goodall' who grew up in Bournemouth.
 
• **Sentence C** will be the next sentence because it further tells us about Jane Goodall. It tells us how she was as a child.
 
• **Sentence B **will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence A** will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **D**: Jane Goodall grew up in the English town of Bournemouth.
 
• **C**: As a child she would wait for hours to observe a chicken laying an egg.
 
• **B**: In 1957, she went to Kenya where she met the British paleoanthropologist, Louis Leakey.
 
• **A**: Impressed with Jane’s patience with animals, he chose her for the mission to understand chimpanzees.

 
 
 
 
 

**​Correct Arrangement:__** *Jane Goodall grew up in the English town of Bournemouth. As a child she would wait for hours to observe a chicken laying an egg. In 1957, she went to Kenya where she met the British paleoanthropologist, Louis Leakey. Impressed with Jane’s patience with animals, he chose her for the mission to understand chimpanzees.*
